title: Runtime kernel advisor for heterogeneous GPUs and variable sequence lengths
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Goal: Build an architecture- and sequence-length-aware kernel selection layer (the "kernel advisor") that automatically picks the best compute kernels for a given model variant, device type (GPU family), batch/seq length distribution, and quantization mode. This reduces per-token latency and increases throughput across our hosted and dedicated fleets while maintaining SLOs and memory safety.

Scope:
- Offline microbench harness to profile kernel permutations (matmul kernels, attention variants, fused kernels) per device and sequence length bucket.
- Runtime advisor: cached lookup + lightweight online sampling to handle distribution drift.
- Integration with prefill/decode scheduling so kernel choice is considered for both prefill (longer seqs) and decode (short seq + KV cache patterns).
- Safety fallbacks: memory-aware checks, compatibility mapping (kernel->quantization support), and graceful downgrade to conservative kernels under memory pressure.

Success metrics:
- Median token latency reduction of >=10% across p50/p95 on mixed workloads on our gpunet pool for seq lengths 32/128/512.
- Throughput gain of >=8% for high-batch generative workloads without increasing OOM rate.
- No increase in error/incorrect outputs attributable to kernel changes; <0.1% rollout rollback rate.

Approach:
1) Design a small canonical feature key: {model-hash, device-class, seqlen-bucket, batch-size-range, quant-mode}. Store best kernel choice and stats per key.
2) Build an offline profiler (bench harness) that runs microbenchmarks across representative models (Llama-family and Mistral-family variants), quant/memory modes, and devices (A100, H100, RTX6000). Output CSV/artifacts ingested into a central recommendations DB.
3) Implement runtime advisor component in serving runtime: on prefill/request, advisor loads candidate kernel list from cache (fast path). If key is missing, fall back to default and enqueue an async sample job to benchmark in background on spare capacity. Sampling respects SLOs and doesn't block requests.
4) Tie advisor to scheduler: if advisor predicts kernel choice that increases memory, scheduler adjusts batch packing and may pick a different kernel tradeoff.
5) Expose opt-in flags in deployment config and a console view for per-model kernel mappings and metrics.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Storage vs lookup granularity: more buckets increase accuracy but increase cache footprint. We will start with 4 seqlen buckets (<=32, 33-128, 129-512, >512) and iterate.
- Offline vs online: offline profiling yields high-quality recommendations but lags behind new models; online sampling closes the loop but must not perturb production. We'll limit live sampling to low-traffic models and use canary routes.
- Kernel variability across driver/CUDA versions: need to tag profiles by driver/driver-hash.

Acceptance criteria:
- Bench harness that can produce per-kernel CSV with stable metrics checked-in and CI-able.
- Runtime advisor integrated and feature-flagged; unit and integration tests for cache correctness and fallback behavior.
- Dashboard with kernel choice distribution and latency delta for top 10 models in dedicated fleet.

Rollout plan:
- Spike -> offline profiling across devices (week 1).
- Implement advisor and unit tests (week 2).
- Canary on <1% traffic for dedicated pool with conservative defaults (week 3).
- Monitor for 72 hours, iterate on buckets and safety checks, expand to 10% if stable (week 4).

Risks:
- Profiles contaminated by background noise: mitigate with repeated runs and median-of-N.
- Regression in correctness due to less-tested kernels: run functional smoke tests and compare logits for a regression set.

Links: confluence spec and design doc, profiling artifacts, and PRs are listed below in comments.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Spike complete: small bench harness implemented that runs matmul/attention kernels across seqlen buckets. Early results show H100 benefits from new fused attention kernel at seqlen >= 256. Artifacts: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-8473+-+Kernel+Advisor+Spike

2026-03-01 - Discussion with scheduler team: agreed advisor will expose a 'predicted_memory_delta' in metadata so scheduler can rebalance batch packing. Action: add memory probe in bench harness. @Daniel Kim to review impact on autoscaler (ENG-8234).

2026-03-05 - Offline profiling run #3 completed across A100/H100/RTX6000 for two model snapshots (mistral-7b, redwood-13b-quantized). Results uploaded to GCS: gs://redwood-inference/profiles/ENG-8473/2026-03-05/. Notable: quantized kernels perform inconsistently on older drivers; will tag by driver hash.

2026-03-09 - Design review with PM (Lena Ortiz) and Security: approved feature-flagged rollout and no additional security review required. Recording: https://meetings.redwood.ai/recordings/eng-8473-design
